# Sirach Chapter 25 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 25 | **Date:** 2026-03-17

---

**25:1** Three things fill me with delight, and they please both God and people: brothers living in harmony, neighbors who love one another, and a husband and wife who are truly matched.

**25:2** Three kinds of people my soul despises, and their very existence offends me: an arrogant poor person, a dishonest rich person, and a lecherous old man who should know better.

**25:3** If you didn't build up wisdom when you were young, what will you have to draw on when you're old?

**25:4** How fitting it is to find sound judgment in a gray-haired person, and wise counsel among respected elders!

**25:5** Wisdom in the elderly is a beautiful thing; discernment and good counsel in people of standing.

**25:6** Experience is the elders' crown; the fear of the LORD is their glory.

**25:7** Nine things I count as blessings in my heart; I'll name the tenth out loud: a man who sees his children thrive; a man who lives long enough to watch his enemies fall;

**25:8** blessed is the man who lives with a sensible wife; the man who has never let his tongue get him into trouble; the man who has never had to serve someone less worthy than himself;

**25:9** blessed is the man who has found good sense; and the man whose words actually reach people who want to hear them;

**25:10** how great a thing it is to find wisdom! But nothing compares to fearing the LORD.

**25:11** The fear of the LORD beats everything. The person who has it — who can you compare them to?

**25:13** Any wound — but not the wound of the heart! Any pain — but not the pain caused by a woman!

**25:14** Any enemy — but not a vengeful hater! Any strike — but not the vengeance of enemies!

**25:15** No head strikes more lethally than a serpent's head; no anger burns more fiercely than an enemy's.

**25:16** I'd rather share a den with a lion and a dragon than live with a vicious woman.

**25:17** A wicked woman's evil shows on her face — she goes around scowling like a bear. Her husband has to face the neighbors looking like a man in mourning clothes.

**25:18** Despair that turns to sighing, a heart that can't lift — this is a wife who brings her husband nothing but gloom.

**25:19** All other evil pales beside the evil of a bad woman. Let sinners get what she deserves.

**25:20** Sandy ground under old feet that won't hold — that's what a nagging wife is to a peaceful man.

**25:21** Don't fall for a woman because she's beautiful; don't set your heart on a woman for her looks.

**25:22** Rage, shamelessness, utter humiliation — that's what it means for a wife to be the one keeping the household going.

**25:23** A broken spirit, a sad face, a wounded heart — the mark of a cruel wife. Weak hands, shaking knees — the husband she can't bring herself to gladden.

**25:24** Sin entered the world through a woman, and because of her we all die.

**25:25** Don't let water find a crack; don't let a bad wife find room to work.

**25:26** If she won't walk beside you, cut her loose.
